note: Testable footprints of publicly documented or alleged organised Wikipedia-editing initiatives on Israel/Palestine/Zionism/Judaism. Written BEFORE running any test (2026-11-06). Each footprint states the prediction that would follow IF the initiative changed English Wikipedia leads at a scale our data can see. A null result does not show an initiative did not exist or did nothing; our lead-event data are blind to who an account is, to talk-page and RfC canvassing, and to edits outside opening paragraphs. Organisation-level only: no account is linked to any person or group. Status: documented = established by a primary record (ArbCom decision, the organisation's own announcement) or by multiple independent reports with the organisation's confirmation; alleged = reported, disputed or unconfirmed. All sources were read as search snippets (page fetches blocked in this session) and must be verified before publication.

data.lead_events: data/mass2_events.json.gz -> articles[title].lead_events[] {ts, term, kind insert|remove, reverted, u (salted hash, linkable only within one article), acct{age_d, lt500, ext, indef}}; groups from data/mass2.json (topic n=4642, comparison n=5678). Critical terms: settler_colonial, apartheid, genocide, ethnic_cleansing, occupation, nakba_expulsion, war_crimes.
data.weekly_edits: data/results.json articles[].w_edits (deep panel, week0 2021-01-01; treatment n=411, clean control n=85)
data.first_sentence: data/ratchet.json articles.Zionism.fs_timeline [date, variant id, reverted] + fs_variants (150 of 169 variants stored)

method_default.statistic: DiD of log rates: log((T_post+1)/(T_pre+1)) - log((C_post+1)/(C_pre+1)), T = topic-lead critical-term events, C = comparison-lead events, pre = 4 weeks before the date, post = the date's week and 3 weeks after
method_default.placebo: 2,000 random dates 2021-07-01..2026-09-01 (global) and dates within +-26 weeks of the event (local); one-sided p in the predicted direction = share of placebo statistics at least as extreme
